decision: NO MATERIAL OBSERVABILITY GAP — RETAIN RESEARCH-ONLY

entries.fact: before/after file additions, deletions, and modifications
entries.v0_boundary: Snapshot schema 2 compares repository-relative entry kind, SHA-256, and byte size; Git/VCS supplies the underlying fact more simply for tracked content.
Deterministic only under strict-utf8-lines-v1; binary, symlink, and special entries contribute zero LOC; Git diff/stat and language tools are established substitutes.

entries.fact: dependency additions, removals, and specification changes
entries.v0_boundary: Covers supported package.json and selected pyproject.toml tables, normalizes names, and hashes specifications; manifest diffs and ecosystem tools expose the same underlying changes with broader language coverage.

Reports byte deltas only for configured relative instruction paths, defaulting to root AGENTS.md and AGENTS.override.md; it does not prove that Codex loaded those bytes. Git, file size, and native instruction inspection are sufficient.
No V0 event records loaded instruction/context bytes or repeated loads.
V0 records only whether a completed turn contains a usage object; it discards input, cached-input, output, and reasoning-output values that current codex exec JSONL documents directly.
Recognizes supplied PreCompact/PostCompact hook names but hook-only input is always degraded and no 0.151.0 live canary was run; Codex hooks and App Server document native compaction events.

Validates thread-start and balanced turn boundaries in one supplied trace but does not retain thread identity or reconstruct cross-file continuation; native thread APIs and logs expose continuation directly.

entries.fact: reopening or rereading after a state transition
entries.v0_boundary: Command hashes are not correlated with paths or compaction/checkpoint transitions; non-shell read inputs are discarded.
V0 has no goal/checkpoint model; current Codex App Server exposes persisted goal state and thread continuation natively.

entries.fact: missing or malformed V0 input coverage
entries.v0_boundary: V0 visibly reports malformed lines, unknown hashed identifiers, missing/invalid fields, sequence imbalance, snapshot warnings, and unavailable usage/command dimensions. This is observer-health normalization, not a new coding-workflow fact.

Equal SHA-256 command summaries can be counted deterministically for observed completed exec commands or hook Bash records, but V0 does not aggregate repetition and live evidence contains only one command; native traces preserve the command and order.
V0 does not retain tool arguments for non-Bash reads and hashes the whole Bash command, so same-path identity is unavailable.
V0 recognizes a web_search item type but does not retain or fingerprint queries; current Codex App Server, Copilot SDK, and trace systems expose search/tool arguments.
Tool and command outputs are neither retained nor fingerprinted.
Duplicate observed command hashes can be a retry proxy, but provider retries, corrected tool arguments, and retry cause are not represented; native/OTel traces expose richer attempt events.
Turn and command counts do not establish that later work corrected earlier work.
Before/after snapshots expose final structural delta, not transient edits, abandonment, or intent.
No event identifies recovery intent; repeated activity remains an unproven proxy.

entries.fact: tests, lint, type checks, and builds executed
entries.v0_boundary: Classifies observed shell command shapes and records program basename, status, and exit code; shell parsing, wrapper commands, non-shell tools, missing events, and hook degradation create false negatives. Native logs and CI are authoritative.
Uses command status/exit code when present; absence is unavailable rather than failure. CI/test output provides the stronger result.
Equal command hashes and verification kinds can be counted from observed summaries, but V0 does not aggregate them and cannot establish equivalent tests with changed arguments.
The command-verification coverage dimension reports unavailable/degraded evidence, but cannot prove verification did not occur outside the supplied trace.
Turn completed/failed and runtime error counts establish protocol termination, not correct or accepted task completion.
Doctor checks only exec JSON and hooks; V0 does not inventory tools. Native configuration, SDK/App Server, and product UIs expose configured tools.

Reliably summarizes observed command executions and counts file-change items; non-Bash hook tool names and exec MCP/web arguments are not emitted in derived output. Native and OTel traces retain richer tool identity/order.
V0 intentionally discards raw output and does not record output byte counts; App Server and trace systems expose output/duration fields.
No tool inventory exists, so exposure cannot be joined to observed use.
V0 has no externally defined expected-tool oracle; invocation frequency cannot establish selection quality.
Exec turn terminal events and supplied SessionEnd hooks expose protocol boundaries with known gaps; native runtimes expose them directly.
No acceptance, evaluator, user approval, test sufficiency, or correctness field exists.
A later prompt or turn is not sufficient to label correction/rejection, and V0 does not retain prompt semantics.
Counts turn.failed and error events and command failures when exposed, but cannot reliably distinguish provider, transport, sandbox, timeout, or task failure from current derived fields.
